courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Principles of Epidemiology for Public Health
courses.description: An introductory course that considers the meaning, scope, and applications of epidemiology to public health practice and the uses of vital statistics data in the scientific appraisal of community health. One lecture and two lab hours per week.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Injury as a Public Health Problem
courses.description: This course examines unintentional injuries from a public health perspective. The course covers core concepts in injury prevention and control, including the epidemiology of unintentional injury, prevention strategies, behavioral models, child and adolescent injury, messaging framing, the Haddon matrix, and injury surveillance.

source.text: EPID 625. | 3 Credits. | Corequisite, EPID 600 . | MHCH 625 , HBEH 625 .

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Violence as a Public Health Problem
courses.description: This course covers core concepts in violence prevention and control, including the epidemiology of violence, prevention strategies for inter-personal and intra-personal violence, behavioral models that describe power structures that reinforce personal and societal factors affecting self-harm and violence towards others, and violence directed towards children and adolescents.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Research in Epidemiology
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. A course for undergraduate students who wish to conduct research as part of an ongoing epidemiology project or as an independent activity.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 3 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Problems in Epidemiology
courses.description: A course for undergraduate students who wish to make an intensive study of some special problems in epidemiology.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 3 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Foundations of Scientific Reasoning in Epidemiology
courses.description: Introduces concepts in logic, probability, statistics, and causality, all from an epidemiologic perspective. Provides an introduction to computer programming for epidemiologists.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: R for Epidemiologists
courses.description: This course is intended to be the most effective and efficient way for UNC Epidemiology students to establish a foundation in the R programming language, RStudio IDE, and functional programming modalities. Special attention is given to R topics and packages relevant for epidemiological data management, analysis, and visualization.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Systematic Review
courses.description: Course gives students background in assessing and conducting systematic reviews. Focuses on 1) reading, discussing, and critiquing systematic reviews on various topics; 2) reading background and methods articles on systematic reviews; 3) developing a focused question for systematic review; and 4) developing a protocol for a systematic review over the semester.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Responsible Epidemiology
courses.description: EPID 704 aims to provide level-setting and foundational content on health equity and social determinants of health, with the goal of facilitating a transition into later health equity content in the other epidemiology methods courses.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Introduction to Deductive and Probability Logic in Epidemiology
courses.description: Permission of the instructor for nonmajors. Covers properties of logical relations, truth tables and Euler diagrams, valid and fallacious arguments, cognitive heuristics and biases, interpretations of probability, the probability calculus, Bayes' theorem, binomial and normal distributions, applications of probability logic and probabilistic fallacies, all in an epidemiologic context.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Fundamentals of Epidemiology
courses.description: An intensive introduction to epidemiological concepts and methods from a perspective of causal inference. This course is for students intending to lead, engage in, collaborate in, or interpret the results of epidemiologic studies. Some familiarity with biomedical concepts may be needed. Three lecture hours a week.
courses.requisites_raw: Corequisites, EPID 712 (EPID PhD students and EPID PhD minor students only); Pre- or corequisite, BIOS 600 or 662 or SPHG 712 or equivalent.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Clinical Measurement and Evaluation
courses.description: Provide a broad-based introduction to the concepts and methods of epidemiology with particular emphasis on their application in clinical research, clinical practice and health care policy.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Readings in Fundamentals of Epidemiology
courses.description: A course applying the concepts and methods introduced in EPID 710 (required co-requisite for EPID 712 ) to readings in the epidemiologic, biomedical, and public health research literature.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Theory and Quantitative Methods in Epidemiology
courses.description: An in-depth treatment of basic concepts and skills in epidemiologic research, including problem conceptualization, study design, research conduct, data analysis, and interpretation. Four lecture hours per week. EPID PhD students and EPID PhD minor students only. Permission of the instructor required for all others.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Epidemiologic Data Analysis
courses.description: Required preparation, documented SAS proficiency. This course is a combined lecture/lab format where students get hands-on experience in the analysis and interpretation of data from cohort and case-control studies. Students may take the SAS exemption exam in lieu of taking EPID 700 , EPID 795 or BIOS 511 .
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, EPID 710 or EPID 711; and EPID 700 or EPID 795 or BIOS 511.

source.text: EPID 716. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, EPID 710 or EPID 711 ; and EPID 700 or EPID 795 or BIOS 511 .

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Advanced Epidemiologic Methods
courses.description: Course covers epidemiologic analysis of time-to-event data and emphasizes weighing threats to the accuracy of inferences. Class time is spent discussing weekly readings and homeworks.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Analytic Methods in Observational Epidemiology
courses.description: This course provides an in-depth treatment of the analysis of data from observational epidemiologic studies, including both tabular and regression modeling approaches, and with an emphasis on the importance of study design in developing and executing an analysis plan. A major focus of the course is the semester-long, independent data analysis project in which students apply and integrate the concepts covered in class to a dataset and research question of their choosing.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Readings in Epidemiologic Methods
courses.description: A discussion in journal-club format of readings in general epidemiologic methods, from problem conceptualization to application of results.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Epidemiologic Research Methods
courses.description: Minimum second-year standing in doctoral (with permission of the instructor) or MSCR program. A course in the design and conduct of epidemiologic research. Each student will comprehensively address the conceptual and practical aspects of developing a high-quality, detailed research proposal. EPID PhD or MSCR majors only.

source.text: EPID 726. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, EPID 715 or EPID 804 .

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Cardiovascular Epidemiology
courses.description: Review of cardiovascular health and disease in populations and their population determinants. Topics include epidemiologic methods, risk factors, strategies for prevention, and a student research project. Three lecture hours per week

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Methods and Applications of Cardiovascular Disease Surveillance
courses.description: This course helps students gain experience critiquing and interpreting national and international cardiovascular disease (CVD) surveillance programs, evaluate recommendations for future CVD surveillance research and policy, and to explore CVD surveillance data sources with hands-on experience with practical aspects of study conduct.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Epidemiology of Stroke
courses.description: This course helps students become familiar with physiologic and pathologic aspects of cerebrovascular diseases, provides opportunity to explore research findings regarding major risk factors for stroke and evidence for prevention strategies, and offers a guided experience in critiquing, synthesizing, and communicating stroke related research findings.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Contemporary Issues in Hypertension Research
courses.description: In this seminar, we examine several contemporary issues related to hypertension research, particularly pertaining to measurement of blood pressure. Each session will begin with an overview, likely didactic, followed by more in-depth discussion of the topics.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Biomarkers in Population-Based Research
courses.description: This course surveys the major issues relevant to the application of biomarkers in epidemiological research, including the logistical hurdles in biospecimen collection and storage, assessments of biomarker quality, analytic issues, and the interpretation of quantitative estimates.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Genetic Epidemiology: Methods and Applications
courses.description: Concepts and methods of genetic epidemiology relevant to the study of complex human diseases, including segregation analysis, linkage analysis, and gene-environment interaction. Includes whole genome approaches, as well as nonhuman systems. Three lecture hours a week.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, BIOS 545 and EPID 715; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites

source.text: EPID 743. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, BIOS 545 and EPID 715 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Fundamentals of Public Health Surveillance
courses.description: This course provides the conceptual foundations and practical skills for designing and implementing surveillance systems, for using surveillance data for the conduct and evaluation of public health programs and research.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Biological Basis of Infectious Disease Epidemiology
courses.description: The purpose of this course is to familiarize students with the biological factors underpinning the epidemiology of infectious diseases. Topics will include emerging and endemic viral and bacterial diseases, innate and adaptive immunity, vaccine and therapeutic development, and the public health challenges of infectious disease response. This course is required of all ID epidemiology PhD students, but students may in rare cases exempt out with the permission of the instructor.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Advanced Methods in Infectious Disease Epidemiology
courses.description: This course covers theories, concepts, study designs, and analytical methods of particular importance in studying infectious outcomes. Teaching methods include lectures, hands-on computer practicals, article discussions, and written assignments.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Introduction to Infectious Disease Epidemiology
courses.description: Alternative coursework or prior experience equivalent to the prerequisites will be considered, and permission to register granted, on a case-by-case basis by the instructor. Permission required for non-majors. This course will cover concepts, theory, study designs, and analytical methods of particular importance in infectious disease epidemiology. Most topics will be introduced with a didactic lecture and readings, followed by an in-class exercise, discussion, or computer practical applying relevant theories, concepts, and methods to specific questions in infectious disease epidemiology.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, EPID 600 or EPID 710 or SPHG 712, AND EPID 751.

source.text: EPID 755. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, EPID 600 or EPID 710 or SPHG 712 , AND EPID 751 .

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Introduction to Infectious Disease Modeling and Simulation in R
courses.description: Basic concepts and skills needed to use R software for infectious disease modeling and simulations. Course involves lectures and coding demonstrations. In assignments, students will implement compartmental and stochastic models and simulate epidemic dynamics. 1 credit hour.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, EPID 751 or "Biological Basis of Infectious Disease Epidemiology" (offered as either EPID 799B or EPID 799C) and EPID 755.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Problem Solving Seminar in Advanced Infectious Disease Epidemiology
courses.description: In this seminar, we will explore how a combination of the biological understanding of disease processes and advanced methods in infectious disease analytics are essential to understanding critical problems in infectious disease, including the interpretation of surveillance data, the design of control measures and projecting the course of epidemics. We will take a ''problem based'' approach to learning about these issues, with a focus on a rotating set of disease systems. Restricted to Epidemiology PhD students, though others may be admitted with permission of the instructors.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Methods and Principles of Applied Infectious Disease Epidemiology
courses.description: This course will cover the interaction between an infectious agent, host, and environment; modes and dynamics of transmission; the role of immunity in infectious disease epidemiology; and disease elimination strategies. Three lecture hours per week.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Methods in Field Epidemiology
courses.description: Course will focus on epidemiological methods required to investigate urgent public health problems. Course covers the skills and tools needed to conduct outbreak investigations and communicate findings to the public. Three lecture hours per week.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Vaccine Epidemiology
courses.description: An overview of vaccinology principles, mechanisms of action, and herd protection, and statistical considerations. Students will obtain understanding of how vaccines are produced by industry, undergo preclinical evaluation, and evaluated for efficacy in clinical trials.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Hospital Epidemiology
courses.description: Comprehensive seminar in hospital infection control. Topics include issues in employee health, surveillance, outbreak investigation, environmental sampling, and policy formation. May be repeated for credit. Two to four seminar hours.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, EPID 710; Permission of the instructor required.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Methods and Issues in Pharmacoepidemiology
courses.description: Required preparation, introductory-level epidemiology and biostatistics. Application of the epidemiologic knowledge, methodology, and reasoning to the study of the effects (beneficial and adverse) and uses of drugs in human populations.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Epidemiologic Research with Healthcare Databases
courses.description: Required preparation, competency in data management with SAS ( BIOS 511 , EPID 700 , or equivalent). Learn how healthcare utilization data are generated and use databases to identify study populations and conduct epidemiologic analysis of the utilization and comparative effectiveness/safety of prescription drugs and healthcare services.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, EPID 710 OR EPID 600 (or equivalent); Demonstrated SAS competency.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Cancer Epidemiology and Pathogenesis
courses.description: Equivalent experience for students lacking EPID 710 . Undergraduate major or strong preparation in the biological sciences required. Permission of the instructor for nonmajors. Emphasis on integration of epidemiologic data with laboratory and clinical research findings. Issues in epidemiologic research design, analysis, and interpretation are presented within the context of substantive epidemiology. Three lecture hours a week.

source.text: EPID 770. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, BIOS 600 and EPID 710 .

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Cancer Epidemiology: Survivorship and Outcomes
courses.description: Students will evaluate the strengths and weaknesses of data sources common to cancer survivorship and outcomes studies, focusing on epidemiologic study designs. The course addresses cancer detection, treatment strategies, medical surveillance, and personal behaviors as determinants for prognosis, late effects, and the long-term health of cancer survivors.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Cancer Prevention and Control Seminar
courses.description: An interdisciplinary overview of cancer prevention and control. Emphasis on projects and activities from perspectives of epidemiology, health behavior and education, and health policy and management. Appropriate research design and methodologies are covered.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Analytical Methods of Cancer Health Equity
courses.description: Permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites. Readings and discussions on classic and contemporary topics in cancer health equity. Two seminar hours per week.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Occupational Epidemiology
courses.description: Required preparation, introductory epidemiology and biostatistics. This course provides a background in the epidemiology of work-related illness and injury and the application of epidemiologic concepts and methods in protecting workers' health and safety.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Environmental Epidemiology
courses.description: Epidemiologic ideas and methods applied to evaluation and control of human health consequences of environmental hazards. Pollution of environmental media and global change are considered from a human-ecological perspective, with local and international examples. Three lecture hours per week.

source.text: EPID 785. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, EPID 710 and BIOS 600 .

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Methods in Environmental Epidemiology
courses.description: This course provides specialized training in epidemiologic methods for addressing the unique challenges of research on the health effects of environmental exposures. Topics include study designs, exposure assessment, biomarkers, exposure mixtures, causal inference, and science communication approaches as applied to environmental health questions.

source.text: EPID 787. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, EPID 710 and BIOS 600 .

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Intervention Epidemiology
courses.description: Epidemiologic methods for evaluating interventions, primarily in infectious disease epidemiology and injury epidemiology. Covers randomized designs, such as community trials, and evaluation of non-randomized interventions, such as policies and laws.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Data in Public Health
courses.description: This course provides students with an overview of public health informatics and includes in-depth discussions on informatics approaches used in developing the public health information systems in use today.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Special Studies in Epidemiology I
courses.description: Experimental course to be offered by faculty to determine the need and demand for the subject. Topics will be chosen by faculty based on current public health issues. One credit option.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 3 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Special Studies in Epidemiology II
courses.description: Experimental course to be offered by faculty to determine the need and demand for the subject. Topics will be chosen by faculty based on current public health issues. Two credits option.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Special Studies in Epidemiology III
courses.description: Experimental course to be offered by faculty to determine the need and demand for the subject. Topics will be chosen by faculty based on current public health issues. Three credits option.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Data Analysis in Oral Epidemiology
courses.description: Required preparation, basic knowledge of SAS. Permission of the instructor. Data analysis project in oral epidemiology: data cleanup, file construction, analysis. For three credit hours, student also completes multivariate analysis with linear, logistic regression. Project to result in publishable paper. Two to three seminar hours a week.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Design of Clinical Research Studies
courses.description: Permission required for nonmajors. Clinical research majors only. The goals of this course are to develop a strong fundamental understanding of the design of clinical research studies; to understand selection of study populations, exposure and outcome measurement, and choice of appropriate measures; to understand ethical oversight, project management and quality control.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Physical Activity Epidemiology and Public Health
courses.description: This course provides an overview of major issues in physical activity measurements, population distribution, correlates, impacts (physically and economically), and public health recommendations. Interventions, including relevant theories, will be reviewed. Three lecture hours per week.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Obesity Epidemiology
courses.description: Examines epidemiology research on the causes, consequences, and prevention of obesity. Emphasis on methodological issues pertinent to obesity research.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Analytical Methods in Nutritional Epidemiology
courses.description: Skills and techniques to study how dietary exposures, physical activity, and anthropometric status relate to disease outcomes. Focus is hands-on data analysis using STATA, and interpretation of results from statistical analysis.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Integrating Social and Biological Perspectives on Human Health
courses.description: Student will learn key theories and methodological approaches for how social processes, socio-spatial organization, and social inequality are associated with health patterns, changes, and disparities; theories/approaches for studying human health from a biological perspective; and strategies using integrated social and biological research perspectives and address advantages and challenges.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Introduction to Social Epidemiology
courses.description: This course provides an overview of key concepts, methods and findings in research on social determinants of population health. Classes will consist of a didactic presentation followed by in-class group work modules and large group summary discussion.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, SPHG 711 or SPHG 712 or EPID 710, or other introductory epidemiology course with instructor permission.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Social Theories for Epidemiologic Research
courses.description: EPID827 explores key social theories and their applications in epidemiologic research. Drawing from interdisciplinary perspectives, students will examine prevailing frameworks outlining how social structures, power dynamics, cultural contexts, and identity shape health behaviors, access to care, and outcomes. By course end, students will be equipped to apply social theory to research design, hypothesis generation, data interpretation, and the development of interventions that address unjust and preventable health outcome differences across socially-defined populations to ensure more rigorous, relevant, and ethical epidemiologic research. Designed for Epidemiology PhD students.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Reproductive and Perinatal Epidemiology
courses.description: Epidemiology of reproductive and perinatal health outcomes, including infertility, fetal loss, preterm birth, birthweight, congenital malformations, and infant mortality. Includes current knowledge regarding epidemiology of these outcomes and discussion of methodologic issues. Three lecture hours per week.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, EPID 600 or EPID 710 or EPID 711 or SPHG 712.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Advanced Research Methods for Reproductive, Perinatal and Pediatric Epidemiology
courses.description: Critical review of current topics in, and methods for, perinatal and pediatric epidemiology.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Teaching Experience in Epidemiology
courses.description: Open to EPID majors, second-year or above. Provides epidemiology majors with supervised experience in teaching and course preparation. Students act as assistants in departmental courses. Two to eight seminar hours a week.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Readings in Epidemiology
courses.description: Permission of the instructor required. Independent reading and tutorial guidance in special areas of epidemiology.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Topics in Epidemiology Seminar
courses.description: EPID majors only. Topics are chosen to reflect emerging issues in the field, as well as those that meet the interests of the students and faculty in the department.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Epidemiology Doctoral Seminar
courses.description: Exposes students to issues and debates in the philosophy of science, the object of knowledge in epidemiology, and the place of epidemiology in public health.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Translating Health Equity Methods into Practice
courses.description: This course builds students' self-efficacy in using frameworks for equity assessment of programs and policies, articulating one's position on health inequity issues as well as in engaging opposing viewpoints. The course will also provide exposure to professionals who are advancing health equity in public health practice and research settings. Students will synthesize knowledge across their equity coursework and use that as a basis to define and build their health equity research or practice work. MPH Health Equity and Social Justice Students only.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 1 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Pharmacoepidemiology Seminar
courses.description: This is a weekly seminar to explore current problems in pharmacoepidemiology. It supplements the introductory course, EPID 765 . Required preparation, basic knowledge of epidemiology and biostatistics. May be repeated. One seminar hour a week.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Infectious Disease Seminar
courses.description: Required preparation, introductory epidemiology and biostatistics. Detailed review of selected topics in infectious disease epidemiology. May be repeated for credit.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Seminar in Oral Epidemiology
courses.description: Explores conceptual and methods issues in conducting epidemiologic investigations of oral conditions, specifically caries, periodontal disease, and oral cancer (topics rotate semesters).

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Advanced Seminar in Cardiovascular Research
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Review of substantive and methodological research in cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases. May be repeated for credit. Two to six seminar hours a week.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Epidemiology Practice
courses.description: Designed to give epidemiology majors a supervised field experience in population health research.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Epidemiology Laboratory Practice
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Students work individually with a faculty member on supervised laboratory research and skills development. May be repeated for credit. Two to 18 laboratory hours a week.

courses.subject: EPID
courses.title: Research in Epidemiology
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Independent investigation in consultation with an instructor who must assign or approve the subject of research. Credits vary according to the effort and rigor of the research.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.
